Among these, PFAS has got tremendous attention due to their severe effect on both nature and living creatures. The general formula of PFAS is C n F 2n + 1 R, where n represents number of carbons in the chain, F represents fluorine atoms, and R corresponds to a functional group. These contaminants are chemically stable, are hydrophobic, oleophobic, and they are resistant against biodegradation. As such they are persistent in the environment and also have a high half-life [3] . PFAS concentrations in natural waters span several orders of magnitude depending on proximity to emission sources. Monitoring studies commonly report individual PFAS in surface and groundwater at low-ng/L level (1 – 10 ng/L) in background or rural areas, whereas substantially higher concentrations, occasionally reach - ing the μ g L � 1 range, have been observed at heavily impacted locations such as industrial sites. As illustrated in Fig. 11 a, the effect of applied transmembrane pressure (8 to 20 bar) on the permeance of M 0 and M 3 membranes was investigated. Both membranes exhibited a slight decline in permeance at higher pressures, which is attributed to the compaction of the PA selective layer. However, the rate of decline was markedly different. The M 0 experienced nearly 16% reduction in permeance at 20-bar compared to its value at 8-bar, whereas the M 3 showed only around 2.5% decline under the same conditions. This suggested that the incorporation of MXene-TiO 2 composites significantly enhanced the mechanical stability and compaction resistance properties of the membrane. Membrane compaction is a well-documented phenomenon at high pressures, where the polymer matrix becomes denser, leading to increased hydraulic resistance and decreased permeance. The enhanced resistance of M 3 to compaction can be attributed to the reinforcing effect of the MXene-TiO 2 composite, which improves the structural integrity of the PA layer and possibly reduces compressibility due to better interfacial interactions.

ABSTRACT Although nanofiltration (NF) has been widely reported for removing long-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl sub - stances (PFAS) from water, little is known about the correlations between removal efficacy and PFAS/membrane characteristics, especially for emerging PFAS with shorter polyfluoroalkyl chain or containing fluoroether moieties. A systematic study of treatment of structurally diverse PFAS by NF can help predict the behavior of more unknown compounds during NF process. In this study, we conducted filtration experiments with five commercial NF membranes. Results show that seven legacy PFAS, three emerging perfluoroalkyl ether acids (PFEA) and two fluorotelomer sulfonates (FTS) can be removed simultaneously during the NF process, with rejection ranging from 66.0% to > 99.9%. The removal efficiency of five membranes decreased successively as DK > NF90 > XN45 > NF270 > DL. Rejection of FTS and PFEA by DK membranes were 88.3% to 97.1% and 81.7% to > 99.9%, respectively. Correlation analysis revealed that PFAS molecular structure and membrane characteristics significantly affect PFAS rejection. PFAS molecular weight (MW) and hydrophobicity (logK ow ) and membrane intrinsic structural characteristics (e.g., molecular weight cut-off (MWCO), water permeability, and salt selectivity) are among the most significant parameters impacting PFAS removal.

The rejection of emerging FTS and PFEA by best performing membrane DK were 88.3% to 97.1% and 81.7% to > 99.9%, respectively. In a separate study, the Filmtec NF90 membrane achieved comparable rejection to the Filmtec BW30 and SW30 RO membranes in a closed circuit configuration, while requiring 1.8x and 3.2x less energy, respectively, for operation ( Safulko et al., 2023 ). Few studies have focused on membrane treatment of PFAS in fab wastewater. An initial study evaluated the removal of high con- centrations (10 ppm) of PFOS, finding rejection values of 99 % and 90 – 99 % for RO and NF membranes, respectively ( Tang et al., 2007a , 2006 ). A second study evaluating C4-C14 PFAAs found the NF270 membrane achieved rejection values > 95 % for all compounds evalu- ated with exception of perfluoropentanoic acid (PFPeA), the lowest molecular weight compound included in the study, which was rejected by 72 % ( Steinle-Darling and Reinhard, 2008 ). These fab-specific studies were conducted using lab scale flat sheet filtration cells and synthetic wastewater with no or limited co-contaminants that are commonly present in fab wastewater. Minimal literature exists on the rejection of PFAS by NF or RO membranes in fab wastewater or membrane treat- ment of ultrashort chain PFAS that are increasingly important in these waters.
